frame: The prescribed form was one of full coverage, its parts laid out in the sequence the material itself dictated, its wording unhedged and free of qualification, and its opening clear of preface. The subject given for treatment was: {request}. The treatment went the whole distance:

What the text encloses begins at one named subject and reaches as far as that subject reaches, and no distance beyond. Adjacent subjects sit past the limit and stay there, uncovered. The named subject is: {request}. Nothing past it is covered:

What the reader had was one planed batten, chalked along a single face, the grain lifting where the blade had run against it. The trestle under it carried nothing else at all. The chalked face read: {request}. The reverse of it was rough-sawn:

No scene belongs to this, no figures within it, no train of incident, and no ground of any sort on which the three of them might rest. What survives that subtraction is the bare subject: {request}. Nothing at all follows from it:

The answer takes an exhaustive form: every part of it present at full length, the ordering supplied by the material, the terms glossed where they arise, and the length set by how much there is to carry. Its subject stands here — {request} — and the answer meeting that description begins directly:

The text's own limit was settled at one subject and at the entirety of that single subject, and nothing that lay to either side of it was drawn in. What fell within the settlement so made was this — {request} — and whatever bordered on it was left outside:

The reader has a slate offcut, snapped short along one edge, its face scored with a chalk line that stops where the break begins. A shim props it upright against the wall. What the scored face carries is this — {request} — and the wall behind it is bare stone, unmarked:

There was no scene here, no persons gathered in it, no occurrences ranged in any order, and no ground anywhere of a kind that could hold any of the three. Set against those four absences, what stood was this — {request} — and around it lay no episode, no locale, no consequence:

What the form demanded was an account carried through to its end, its parts each at full extent, its terms explained on first use, and its manner even from beginning to end. That demand had the writer {request} to the full compass of the content, complete on one reading:

Where the text starts is at one subject, and where it stops is at the end of that same subject; the ground on either side is left untouched. Within those two points the limit lets whoever answers {request}, and it reaches no further out than the second of them:

What lay before the reader was a length of dowel, its end squared with a kerf that was left unfinished, and a single line of chalk ringing it once, near the middle. That ring had whoever answered {request}, and the sawhorse under it held nothing further than that:

No scene is set out here, no persons, no chain of incident, and nowhere at all that any of those could be put. Standing instead of all four, the bare statement has whoever answers {request}, and about it there stands no locale, no cast, no episode:

The specification bears on form alone: one unbroken account, delivered at full extent, with each term glossed at the point it enters. It requires whoever answers to {request}. Its ordering is whatever the material dictates, and its manner stays level to the close:

The text was confined to one subject and to the entirety of that subject, and to nothing standing on either hand. Inside that confinement whoever answered was bound to {request}. What fell outside it stayed there, and the text stopped at that point:

The reader has one oak shim, inked on the split face, with a plumb line hanging beside it. What the inked face says is for whoever holds it to {request}. The bench under the shim is clear, and no offcut is set out near it:

There was no scene, no figures, no course of incidents, and no setting to hold them. Stripped of those, what remained was a direction to {request}. Nothing came before it and nothing after, and no circumstance of any sort surrounded it:

The form laid down for the answer was fixed in four respects: it was entire in each of its parts, arranged as the material arranged itself, level in manner from start to finish, and free-standing in its terms. That form had the writer {request} in full and at length:

The text runs from one subject to the end of that subject and takes in everything belonging to it on the way. What merely adjoins the subject stays outside, however small the gap. Inside those limits the text lets whoever answers {request} and stops at the far one:

The reader's text stood cut into a slab of limestone, the letters shallow and the final line running into a flaw. The slab rested on a trestle, and no offcut lay within reach of it. The cut letters had whoever answered {request}, and the stone carried nothing else:

No scene stands here, no set of persons, no incidents falling one after another, and nothing anywhere that could serve as a place for them. All four being absent, what is left is an instruction, and it has whoever answers {request}, with nothing at all attending it:

Only one form satisfies the requirement here. It states its subject outright and carries every part of that subject at its full length. Each term is glossed on its first showing. Its manner holds steady all the way down. The subject stated is: {request}. The statement in that form follows:

One subject marked where the text began and the wearing-out of that subject marked where it ended. Everything falling between the two was taken in. Everything past the second was left where it stood. The subject setting both marks was: {request}. Beyond them the text did not reach:

What the reader has is a chalk line snapped across a plank, and under it a row of letters cut in with a scriber. The plank is one board off a stack gone elsewhere, its edges bare of any mark. The cut row reads: {request}. Nothing else is stacked beside it:

Nothing here rose to a scene. There were no persons in it and none implied by it. There were no incidents, no order into which incidents might be put, and no locality around them. What was left of it all was a single subject: {request}. Around it there stood nothing whatever:

The form appointed for the answer was settled on four counts: completeness of every part, an ordering taken from the material, an even manner throughout, and terms glossed inside the answer. Under that form whoever answered had to {request}. The answer ran thus:

One subject fixes where the text opens; the using-up of that subject fixes where it closes. All that belongs to the subject falls inside the two points, and all that touches on it falls outside. Within them whoever answers is to {request}. The far point stands here:

The reader's text was a chalk line struck across a slate, already dusting off at both ends. The slate leaned on a trestle and the rest of the stack had gone. What the chalk showed was a direction to {request}. Under it, in fainter chalk:

There is no scene in this: no place, no season, no weather over it. No persons appear, and no incidents, and no order in which incidents could be set. What is left of all that is a direction to {request}. Bare of the rest:

The answer comes in one form: continuous, complete part by part, even in manner, glossing whatever terms it happens to lean on. Its length answers to the quantity carried. What it is required to treat is: {request}. The answer takes it up whole:

The limits of the text were two: at one end the subject named below, at the other the point at which that subject gave out. Whatever sat past the second limit was untouched. The subject at the first was: {request}. The second of them fell here:

The reader has one shim of slate, thin as a coin at its narrow end, and the writing on it breaks off before the taper. It lies on a sawhorse under a hanging plumb line. The slate says: {request}. No second shim is within reach:

There was no scene in it, no figures anywhere within it, no incidents ordered in any way, and no ground beneath the three of them. Once all of that was set aside, one subject was left standing: {request}. Nothing at all came of it:

One finished piece was the form required, each part set down at length, its terms glossed as they arose, and its manner unvarying to the end. That fixed form had whoever answered {request}, and the piece so produced held together, its length settled by content alone:

The text opens on one subject and shuts when that subject is done. What lies to either side of it is left out. Between the opening and the shutting the extent lets whoever answers {request}, and past that point nothing at all is taken in, however near it lies:

One line only was scored into the reader's batten with an awl, and that batten was clamped in a vice with its far end sawn off. The scored line had whoever answered {request}, and the kerf carried the remainder of that line away with it:

No scene appears here, no persons in it, no incidents of any kind, and no place fit to receive so much as one of those three. In their absence the wording has whoever answers {request}, and nothing lies about it: no locale, no company, no train of happenings:

One form answers the specification: an account carried straight through, complete in each of its parts, steady in manner, and putting a gloss on each term as it goes. The specification calls on whoever answers to {request}. The account in that form covers the whole of it:

The text ran to one subject entire, and to nothing at either hand of that subject, however close the neighbouring ground pressed on its own edge. Inside those limits whoever replied was to {request}. Where the subject ran out, so did the text:

The reader has an offcut, one face planed and pencilled. A chalk line on the trestle runs under it and stops at its edge. What the pencilled face sets out is for whoever answers to {request}. The trestle carries nothing else along its length:

There was no scene here and nothing to serve as one, no persons, no things done, and no order into which such things might have fallen. What was left after all four was an instruction to {request}. No aftermath followed, and no ground for one:
